gen-gf-dekko-general-sans: General Sans draws its sans-serif lines with steady pressure and a tall x-height that fills the line, while Dekko above it looks scribbled by hand. Dekko is the loose one; General Sans keeps things tidy.
gen-gf-dekko-manrope: Calipers-shaped c's and a squat, brush-pen belly give Dekko a casual, hand-lettered look. Manrope follows with bright open curves and a single steady line width, a tidy sans for the quieter text.
gen-gf-dekko-montserrat: Hand-lettered charm meets wire-smooth lines. Dekko's pen-and-paper looseness feels relaxed beside Montserrat, whose wide, glide-like curves and oversized counters make the sans-serif body feel crisp and geometric.
gen-gf-dekko-satoshi: Loose, friendly handwriting up top. Satoshi's soaring x-height and wide-open e keep the plain sans body easy to follow, so a moderate body size should be plenty.
gen-gf-dekko-switzer: Switzer has wire-like, tubular letters with a tall waist line. Dekko earns its keep big and short, where its caliper-shaped c and brush-pen belly get room to show off.
gen-gf-dekko-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern and crisp, its plain sans letters carrying a high mean line and crossbars as heavy as the stems. And Dekko's handwritten looseness would feel a bit much over a long page, so brief copy suits it better.
gen-gf-dela-gothic-one-fs-karma: Big, loud and blocky on top. Dela Gothic One hits hard with its nearly capital-height lowercase, while Karma, a serif with slight stroke contrast, steadies everything beneath it.
gen-gf-dela-gothic-one-fs-paquito: Commanding Dela Gothic One fills its lines with wide, heavy shapes and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Paquito, a classic serif, does the gentler work, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-fs-familjen-grotes: Delius Unicase writes in relaxed, untapered strokes with a pronounced x-height. Familjen Grotesk sits below as a plain sans, lively and a touch narrower, and the two share the page easily.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-fs-hind: Relaxed handwriting with rope-ladder spacing leads the way, its strokes never tapering. And Hind, a sans with a drawn-string steadiness and lowercase nearly matching its capitals, keeps the text grounded.
